task.description: Root-cause ISS-0396: Ecto.Multi {:task_records, parent_instance_id} collision when TWO OR MORE SUB_PROCESS children spawned in the same hop chain (e.g. via a prior PARALLEL_GATEWAY split) each complete synchronously in the same parent transaction -- distinct from ISS-0392 (already fixed: the call(1)-vs-call(2) collision). Diagnosis only -- route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design.

result.summary:
1) EXACT MECHANISM -- confirmed by reading the merged ISS-0392 code directly (not by trusting the issue's prose alone). `Letflow.Engine.build_complete_task_tail_multi/6` (engine.ex:2419-2518) computes `skip_task_activation?` (engine.ex:2451-2454) -- true iff ANY entry of `prepared_children` has `child_initial_state.status == :completed` -- and uses it solely to decide whether `build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/4` (call (1)) appends its own `{:task_records, parent_instance_id}` step. That predicate is a single yes/no gate over the WHOLE hop chain; it has no per-child mechanism at all. The step actually colliding is built later, in `append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6` (engine.ex:2525-2545), which does `Enum.reduce(prepared_children, multi, fn {parent_token_record_id, prepared}, acc_multi -> SubProcess.append_start_multi(acc_multi, ...) end)` -- i.e. it chains ONE `SubProcess.append_start_multi/7` call per prepared child onto the SAME accumulating `Multi`, unconditionally, for however many children the hop chain spawned. `SubProcess.append_start_multi/7` (sub_process.ex:398-479) ends by calling `maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6` (sub_process.ex:481-508), whose `:completed`-matching clause fires once per child whose `child_initial_state.status == :completed` and appends (via `Multi.merge/2`) a nested completion multi built by `append_completion_multi/5` -> `build_completion_multi_from_merge/12` -> `build_completion_write_steps/12` (sub_process.ex:944-1011). `build_completion_write_steps/12` calls `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6` (sub_process.ex:966-972), which appends `Multi.run(multi, {:task_records, instance_id}, ...)` (task_activation.ex:258) keyed ONLY on `instance_id = parent_token.instance_id`. When a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split spawns 2+ sibling SUB_PROCESS children of the SAME parent instance and 2+ of them have START->END (synchronously-completing) child graphs, each sibling has its OWN `parent_token` (distinct `TokenRecord.id`, one per fork branch) but the SAME `parent_token.instance_id`. Each sibling's own `maybe_chain_synchronous_completion` clause -> `build_completion_write_steps/12` call therefore independently appends its OWN `{:task_records, parent_instance_id}`-keyed step onto the SAME `acc_multi` the `Enum.reduce` in `append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6` is threading through all siblings. At `Ecto.Multi` EXECUTION time (`Repo.transaction/2` -> `apply_operations/5`), sibling 1's nested merge runs first and registers `{:task_records, parent_instance_id}` in the running `names` set; when sibling 2's own nested `Multi.merge/2` callback (built and run later in the same reduce/operations order) tries to fold in its own step under the identical key, `Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3` raises `RuntimeError: cannot merge Multi; ... [task_records: "<parent_instance_id>"]` -- the exact 'cannot merge Multi' shape named in the issue, but a call(2)-vs-call(2) collision, not call(1)-vs-call(2).

2) WHETHER ISS-0392's FIX EXTENDS NATURALLY -- confirmed it does NOT, and structurally cannot without change: ISS-0392's `skip_task_activation?` predicate (§2.2 of lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md) is a single boolean, evaluated once, deciding whether ONE specific step (call (1), `build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi`) is built at all. It has no way to arbitrate among MULTIPLE call(2)-shaped invocations that all target the same key -- there is no 'first sibling wins, skip the rest' concept anywhere in the current code, and even if there were, skipping a later sibling's `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records` call would silently drop that sibling's own newly-pending-task-node inserts (each sibling's cascade computes ITS OWN diff against a freshly re-read parent snapshot via `load_parent_context/2`, sub_process.ex:719/758, which correctly sees the PRIOR sibling's already-applied writes within the same open transaction -- confirmed by `append_completion_multi/5`'s own moduledoc, sub_process.ex:717-720: 'always invoked from a point already inside an open transaction', using `Letflow.Repo` directly so it shares the transaction's connection). So each sibling's write IS semantically necessary and non-redundant -- the diagnosis is NOT 'redundant work that can be skipped', it is 'legitimate sequential writes whose Multi step KEY happens to be too coarse (parent-instance-scoped) to admit more than one occurrence per transaction'. `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6`'s own docstring (task_activation.ex:233-240) states the key is namespaced by `instance_id` specifically so the function 'can be called more than once on the same outer Multi within one transaction (once for the completing task's own instance, once per sub-process completion-cascade level for that level's ancestor instance)' -- this reasoning covers ISS-0392's one-child-per-level case and the distinct-instance_id multi-level cascade case (parent -> grandparent, sub_process.ex:1013-1063, `maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6`, confirmed each level targets a genuinely distinct `instance_id` per §3.1 of the ISS-0392 design doc) but was never extended to cover 2+ SIBLINGS at the SAME level sharing the SAME `instance_id`. This is the genuinely different shape flagged in the task brief: the fix needs a per-invocation-unique Multi key (e.g. keyed by `{instance_id, parent_token.id}` or `{instance_id, child_instance_id}`), not a per-instance boolean skip.

3) CONCRETE FIX PROPOSAL for CODE-DESIGNER (not prescribed code, a scoped direction from reading the real call graph): make the Multi key `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6` uses collision-proof per invocation instead of collision-proof only per ancestor instance. The cleanest lever is in `build_completion_write_steps/12` (sub_process.ex:944-1011), which already has `parent_token` in scope and already builds several OTHER keys off `parent_token.id` (`reconciliation_key = {:sub_process_parent_token_reconciliation, parent_token.id}`, `event_key = {:sub_process_completed_event, parent_token.id}`, `projection_key = {:sub_process_parent_projection, parent_token.id}`, `cascade_lookup_key = {:sub_process_grandparent_lookup, parent_instance_id}` at sub_process.ex:960-963) -- those four never collide across siblings today because each sibling has a distinct `parent_token.id` (one per fork branch). Only the `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records` call (sub_process.ex:966-972) is the outlier, keyed just on `instance_id`. `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6`'s own `Multi.run` key at task_activation.ex:258 would need to become `{:task_records, instance_id, parent_token.id}` (or equivalent per-branch disambiguator threaded in as a new parameter) rather than `{:task_records, instance_id}` alone -- this is a signature change to `append_multi_from_existing_records/6` (new disambiguator parameter) and its one call site in `build_completion_write_steps/12`. Note this key must ALSO stay distinct from `build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi`'s call(1) key (still bare `{:task_records, parent_instance_id}` when `skip_task_activation?` is false) and from deeper cascade levels' own calls (which already use distinct `instance_id`s per §3.1) -- CODE-DESIGNER should re-verify no accidental re-collision is introduced between a disambiguated sibling key and call (1)'s or the cascade's own keys (e.g. by choosing a disambiguator, such as `parent_token.id`, that is never equal to a bare instance_id/atom in a way `Ecto.Multi`'s key equality could conflate -- tuples of different arity/shape are already how ISS-0392's own fix avoided this, so a 3-tuple vs. a 2-tuple key should be safe, but this is CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's to confirm against real `Ecto.Multi` key-equality semantics, not assumed here). Whether the disambiguator should be `parent_token.id`, `child_instance_id`, or a synthetic per-reduce-iteration index is CODE-DESIGNER's call -- `parent_token.id` is attractive because it is already in scope at every call site that needs it and is already used for the four sibling keys above (consistency), but `child_instance_id` is also already threaded through the same call chain and may read more naturally for future maintainers. Alternative NOT recommended: reordering or serializing siblings some other way -- the sequential-transaction ordering is already correct (point 2 above) and is not the defect; only the key's granularity is.

4) EXISTING TEST COVERAGE -- confirmed via `grep` and reading `test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs`'s `describe "ISS-0392 -- a synchronously-completing SUB_PROCESS child no longer collides on {:task_records, parent_instance_id}"` block (line 1022): it contains exactly two tests -- `"single-level: gate completion cascades through synchronous child completion, no raise, no orphan task row"` (line 1023, ONE synchronous child) and `"multi-level cascade: two synchronous SUB_PROCESS completions in one transaction, distinct instance_ids never collide"` (line 1100, a PARENT->GRANDPARENT cascade -- two DISTINCT `instance_id`s at two different ancestor LEVELS, per the ISS-0392 design doc's own §5 point 7 and §3.2's explicit note that this variant 'is expected to pass post-fix purely because distinct keys never collide -- it is not exercising the predicate a second time'). Neither test constructs a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split with 2+ SIBLING SUB_PROCESS children sharing the SAME parent `instance_id` at the SAME level -- i.e. ISS-0396's exact scenario has zero existing coverage anywhere in the suite, confirming both the issue's own stated repro target and ISS-0392's own design doc OQ-2 (renumbered from Revision 1's OQ-4), which flagged self-ancestor/sibling-shaped collisions as an explicitly-unresolved gap rather than a silently-assumed-safe case.

5) INTERACTION WITH ISS-0397 -- confirmed DISTINCT, no shared mechanism, safe to design/fix independently, but same file family. Read docs/issues/ISS-0397.yaml (status: resolved, merged in WF03-ISS0397-20260901): that fix persists `join_counters` durably on `instance_projections` (new column) and rewires `reconcile_projection/5` (the write site) and `build_instance_state/3` (the read site) -- both in `lib/letflow/engine.ex`, NOT in `lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex`. ISS-0396's colliding call site (`build_completion_write_steps/12`'s `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records` call) writes `tasks` rows and does not touch `join_counters` or call `Letflow.Engine.reconcile_projection/5` at all -- `build_completion_write_steps/12`'s own `projection_key` step calls `reconcile_parent_projection/5` (a distinct, `sub_process.ex`-local function), which per this diagnosis is keyed by `parent_token.id` and does not collide today. ISS-0397's fix does not touch `sub_process.ex`, does not change any Multi key shape, and does not change `prepared_children`/`child_initial_state` semantics. The only overlap is that both defects surface via `Letflow.Engine.complete_task/3` and both were discovered around the same PARALLEL_GATEWAY-split work (REQ-208/REQ-062) -- CODE-DESIGNER does not need to coordinate the two fixes' mechanisms, but should be aware ISS-0397's `join_counters` column write happens on the same locked `instance_projections` row `reconcile_parent_projection/5` also updates for each sibling in ISS-0396's scenario, so a regression test exercising 2+ synchronous siblings post-ISS-0396-fix will also incidentally exercise ISS-0397's join_counters persistence on that same row across multiple sequential writes within one transaction -- worth a passing note to TEST-DESIGNER, not a design coupling.
result.recommendation_to_orch: Route to Step 2 CODE-DESIGNER: design a fix that replaces `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6`'s current per-ancestor-instance-only Multi key (`{:task_records, instance_id}`, task_activation.ex:258) with a per-invocation-unique key (e.g. `{:task_records, instance_id, parent_token.id}` or `{:task_records, instance_id, child_instance_id}`) so that 2+ SUB_PROCESS siblings spawned from the same PARALLEL_GATEWAY split, sharing the same parent `instance_id` but each with a distinct `parent_token`, no longer collide when each completes synchronously within the same transaction. This requires a signature change to `append_multi_from_existing_records/6` (new disambiguator parameter, threaded from `build_completion_write_steps/12` at sub_process.ex:966-972 which already has `parent_token` in scope) -- `append_multi/6`'s own single-call-site fixed-atom key (task_activation.ex:176) is confirmed unaffected and should stay untouched. CODE-DESIGNER must also re-verify (and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must re-check) that the new disambiguated key can never accidentally collide with call (1)'s own bare `{:task_records, parent_instance_id}` key (when `skip_task_activation?` is false) or with a deeper cascade level's own call using a distinct `instance_id` -- this diagnosis believes it is safe by construction (different tuple arity/shape) but does not treat that as proven. ISS-0392's own build-time `skip_task_activation?` predicate and its existing tests are confirmed unaffected and should not be modified by this fix. Flag for TEST-DESIGNER: no existing test exercises 2+ sibling SUB_PROCESS children (same parent instance, same level, both synchronously completing) -- new coverage is required, following the same pre-fix-fails/post-fix-passes structure as ISS-0392's own `test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` tests (a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split into 2 branches, each pointing at a `START -> END` child definition, completed in one `complete_task/3` hop chain). Confirmed no shared mechanism with the already-merged ISS-0397 (join_counters persistence, different file/data structure) -- safe to design and implement independently, though a passing note to TEST-DESIGNER that the new regression test will incidentally exercise ISS-0397's join_counters column write on the shared, sequentially-updated `instance_projections` row is worth carrying forward, not a design coupling.
